test: For every short line (fulfilment='short', qty_shipped=0), look for a later order line (any branch, any fulfilment that shipped) by the same customer for the same SKU within 10 operating days (day+1..day+10; also same-day other orders). Share of short lines with no such re-order = candidate lost share. Break down by year, branch, category, customer concentration, and compare to a baseline: how often the same customer orders the same SKU within 10 days after a NON-short line (to separate re-order from ordinary repeat buying). Also check whether the same order carried a transfer/special line for the same SKU.
support: Most short lines (>50%) have no same-customer same-SKU re-order within 10 days, and the re-order rate after short lines is not much higher than the baseline repeat rate after filled lines.
weaken: Most short lines are followed within days by a re-order of the same SKU, at a rate well above the baseline repeat rate, or are covered on the same order by a transfer/special line.
expect: Moderate confidence that most short lines are NOT re-ordered within 10 days (customers buy many SKUs infrequently), so the hypothesis will nominally hold; but the baseline comparison matters: if the re-order rate after short is only modestly above baseline, the 'lost' share is an upper bound and the uplift over baseline is the recovered share. Also suspect synthetic-data artefacts (e.g., uniform rates across years/branches).
